newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended higher on Wednesday, tracking buoyant European debt markets and amid relief that the market painlessly digested a large tranche of new Treasury bonds issued at auctions on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"In two days the Spanish Treasury allotted bonds worth more than 750 billion pesetas, and the market, though not as strong as its Italian counterpart, is really strong," a dealer said.
If the U.S. Federal Reserve leaves its official rates unchanged as is widely expected, the Spanish market is positioned to show further gains on Thursday, Madrid-based dealers said.
Early on Thursday, the market's focus will remain on the Bank of Spain's repo, despite a general consensus that the central bank will leave its monetary policy unchanged.
A Reuters poll showed that among ten financial experts, not one was expecting a rate cut.
But positive remarks on the Spanish economy by the central bank governor Luis Angel Rojo were read by one dealer as opening the door to a more aggressive policy.
"His speech was so positive that I would not be surprised by a lowering," he told Reuters. But others maintained their position saying the economic recovery suggested steady rates.
